Q_001,How do I get help for food like SNAP or other places?,"## Getting Food Assistance in California

You can get help right away and also apply for a longer‑term program that works like **SNAP** (called **CalFresh** in California). Below is a simple guide to the main options, who can apply, what you need, and how to start.
### 1. CalFresh (California’s SNAP)

column3: Monthly benefit that is loaded onto an **EBT card** to buy groceries at any store or farmer’s market.

• U.S. citizens, qualified non‑citizens, and many legal immigrants.
• Adults (18+) or households with children.
• Income must be at or below the state’s limit (about 138 % of the federal poverty level).
• You can still qualify if you are unemployed, receiving unemployment benefits, or have very low earnings.

• Photo ID (driver’s license, state ID, or passport).
• Social Security number (or proof you’re not eligible for one).
• Proof of residence (lease, utility bill, or letter from a shelter).
• Recent pay stubs, unemployment award notice, or bank statements showing income.
• Proof of expenses (rent/mortgage, utilities, medical bills) – helps if you need a larger benefit.

1. **Online** – go to **[BenefitsCal.com](https://www.benefitscal.com)** or **[GetCalFresh.org](https://www.getcalfresh.org)** and create an account.
2. **Phone** – call the CalFresh Benefits Helpline **1‑877‑847‑3663** for assistance or to request a paper application.
3. **In person** – visit your **County Social Services Agency** (the office that handles CalFresh).
4. **Mail** – download a paper form from the agency’s website and mail it in.

• An intake interview (phone or in‑person) to verify information.
• A **30‑day eligibility determination** (most applicants hear back within 2‑3 weeks).
• If approved, the first EBT card is mailed within about **7‑10 days**.
Every California county runs its own CalFresh office, so **hours, wait‑times, and required forms can vary**.  Call your local office or check the county website for the most accurate details.

### 2. Emergency Food Assistance Program (EFAP)

Q_002,Can I recieve multiple types of assistance at the same time?,"## Quick Answer

**Yes.** In California you can often receive more than one public‑assistance benefit at the same time (for example, Medicaid + CalFresh + CalWORKs).  Each program has its own rules, so you’ll need to apply for each one and let the agencies know about any other aid you’re getting.
## How Multiple Programs Work

column1: **Key points**
* Most cash‑aid programs (CalWORKs, GA, CAPI) are **not** “stacked” – you usually receive the **highest** amount you qualify for, but you can still get **other** non‑cash benefits at the same time.
* Some programs treat other benefits as **income** (e.g., UI may affect CalWORKs cash amount).  The agency will calculate your payment accordingly.
* **Lifeline** is a discount program, not cash, so it can be added on top of any other aid you receive.
## Steps to Apply for Multiple Benefits
1. **Gather basic documents**
* Photo ID (driver’s license, state ID, or passport)
* Proof of California residence (utility bill, lease, or mail)
* Social Security Number (or proof of ineligibility if you’re undocumented)
* Recent pay stubs or proof of unemployment (UI award notice)
* Recent tax return or W‑2s (if you have them)
2. **Start with the program you need most**
* **If you lost your job**, apply for **Unemployment Insurance** right away at [UI Online](https://edd.ca.gov).
* While UI is processing, begin applications for **Medi‑Cal** and **CalFresh** (both can be started at the same time).
3. **Apply for cash aid** (if needed)
* **CalWORKs** – apply online at [BenefitsCal.com](https://benefitscal.com) or at your county social‑services office.
* **General Assistance** – contact your county office; many counties let you apply online, by phone, or in person.
4. **Add supplemental programs**
* **Lifeline** – once you have proof of any qualifying program, apply at the Lifeline website or through your phone carrier.
* **SSI or SSDI** – if you are disabled or elderly, call the Social Security Administration or use the online portal.
5. **Tell each agency about the other benefits**
* When you fill out any application, there will be a question asking if you receive other assistance.  Answer truthfully; the agency will adjust your payment if needed.
6. **Follow up**
* Most agencies will schedule an intake interview (in person or by phone).
* Expect a decision within **2–4 weeks** for most cash programs; health and food benefits can be approved faster (often within 1–2 weeks).

## County‑Specific Note

California has **58 counties**, each with its own social‑services office. While the basic eligibility rules are set by the state, **application forms, office hours, and some income limits may differ locally**.
* **Call your county office** (or visit the county website) to confirm:
* Required paperwork
* Whether you can submit applications online or must appear in person
* Any local “time‑limit” rules for cash aid (some counties apply a 3‑month rule for employable adults).
You can find your county’s contact information at the **California Department of Social Services** site: https://www.cdss.ca.gov/County-Contact-Info
## Other Programs Worth Checking
* **Covered California** – health insurance marketplace; you may qualify for subsidies or free Medi‑Cal if your income is low.
* **Workforce Development Programs** – job‑training, apprenticeships, and rapid‑re‑employment services (CalJOBS, local Employment Development Districts).
* **Emergency Rental Assistance (ERA)** – help paying rent if you’re newly unemployed.
* **Utility Assistance (LIHEAP)** – helps with heating or electric bills; eligibility can vary, so call your local energy agency.
* **Veterans Benefits** – if you served, you may be eligible for additional cash, health, or housing aid.
## Bottom Line

You *can* receive several forms of assistance at the same time in California. Start with the program that will give you the fastest cash (UI) and health coverage (Medi‑Cal), then layer on food assistance (CalFresh), cash aid (CalWORKs or GA), and discounts (Lifeline). Keep copies of all paperwork, tell each agency about the other benefits you have, and stay in touch with your local county office for any county‑specific details.
If you have more questions or need help filling out an application, most counties offer free **SSI/SSDI and CAPI advocacy** services—just ask for a “client advocate” when you call.

## 1. Call **211** (or dial **211** from any phone)
1. Tell the operator you need **rent‑assistance**.
2. Be ready to answer basic questions:
* Where you live (address or ZIP)
* How much rent you owe / monthly rent amount
* Your household income and any dependents
3. The specialist will give you the phone number or website for the **county‑specific emergency rental assistance program** and may set up a referral right away.
*You can also start online at the national 211 site: [211.org – Housing Expenses](https://www.211.org/get-help/housing-expenses).*
## 2. Apply for **Emergency Rental Assistance (ERA)**
### Who can apply?
* Residents of the county who have **experienced a loss of income** (job loss, reduced hours, illness, etc.).
* Must be **lawfully present** in the U.S. (citizens, permanent residents, certain visa holders).
* Income limits vary, but most counties use a **percentage of the area median income (AMI)** (often 80 %–150 % of AMI).
### What you’ll need (keep copies ready)

column1: ### Steps
1. **Find the application portal** – the 211 operator or your county website will give you the link.

4. **Upload or mail the required documents**.
5. **Submit** and keep a copy of the confirmation number.
### What happens next?
* A case worker reviews your file (usually within a couple of weeks).
* If approved, the agency **direct‑pay** your landlord or sends you a check for the approved amount.
* Some counties allow you to request **additional months** if you still need help after the first payment.
## 3. If You Need Ongoing Help – **CalWORKs**
1. Call your **County Human Services Agency** (the number is on the CalWORKs website).
2. Request a **CalWORKs interview** (in‑person, phone, or video).
3. Bring the same documents listed above plus **any proof of assets** (bank statements, vehicle registration).
4. If approved, you’ll receive a monthly cash benefit that can be used for rent, utilities, food, etc.
*Processing can take up to 30 days, but you may get **emergency cash** while your case is under review.*

Losing a job can feel overwhelming, but California has a number of programs that can give you money, training, or other support while you look for work.
### 1. **Unemployment Insurance (UI) – State Benefits**

column3: Weekly cash payments while you’re unemployed and looking for work

Most people who have earned wages and lost their job through no fault of their own (layoff, reduced hours, quitting for a good reason, being fired, or being mis‑classified as an independent contractor).

1. Gather required info (see below).
2. **Apply online** at the EDD portal – [edd.ca.gov/unemployment](https://edd.ca.gov/en/unemployment/).
3. Register for a free **CalJOBS** account (the EDD needs this to match you with job openings).
4. Certify each week you’re still unemployed (online or by phone).

• Social Security number
• Driver’s license or ID number
• Last employer’s name, address, and phone
• Last dates worked and reason you left
• Most recent pay stub or W‑2 (if you have it)

• Application is reviewed within a few days.
• First benefit payment usually arrives **within 2‑3 weeks** after you file your first certification, but timing can vary by county.
Some counties have local outreach centers that can help you fill out the UI application in person or by phone. Call your county’s **EDD office** for details.

### 1. Basic Program Facts

column3: Any California resident who meets income and residency rules. You may qualify even if you are not a U.S. citizen, as long as you have a lawful immigration status (or meet certain immigrant‑specific rules).

Q_007,What are the income limits for Unemployment Insurance?,"## Unemployment Insurance (UI) – How Income Affects Eligibility
**Unemployment Insurance in California does not have a fixed “income limit” that says you are *too* high‑earning to apply.**
Instead, the program looks at **how much you earned during your “base period”** (the 12‑month period before you filed your claim) to decide:

column3: What it means for you
You must have earned enough wages in the base period to qualify. The exact amount varies each year, but most workers who earned at least a few hundred dollars per week during that time are eligible.
Your weekly UI payment is a percentage of your recent earnings, up to a state‑wide maximum (about **$450 per week** in 2025). If you earned a very high wage, you will still receive the capped amount.
You can work **part‑time** and still get a reduced UI benefit. The EDD will subtract a portion of your earnings each week from your UI payment.

column1: ### Key Eligibility Points
1. **Base‑Period Requirement**
- The standard base period is the **first four quarters of the last five completed calendar quarters** before you file.
- You need **minimum wages** (generally a few hundred dollars total) in that period.
2. **Being “Able and Available” for Work**
- You must be physically able to work, available for suitable jobs, and **actively looking for work each week**.
3. **Weekly Certification**
- After you’re approved, you certify each week (online, by phone, or by mail) that you are still eligible and report any earnings.
4. **Processing Time**
- It usually takes **about 3 weeks** from the date you file until the first payment is made, assuming no missing information.

column1: ### Quick FAQ
- **Do I need to earn a certain amount to *receive* UI?**
You need enough earnings in the base period to qualify, but there is **no upper earnings cap**—if you earned a high wage, you’ll receive the maximum weekly benefit amount.
- **Can I work part‑time and still get UI?**
Yes. Report any earnings each week; UI will be reduced but not eliminated unless you earn above the “earned income exemption” amount (the first $100 of weekly earnings is usually exempt).
- **What if I’m not sure I qualify?**
The safest step is to **apply**. The Employment Development Department (EDD) will tell you whether you meet the wage‑base requirement and any other eligibility criteria.
**You’re not alone in this transition.** If you need help filling out forms, locating local resources, or just want to discuss what steps make the most sense for you, reach out to:
- **Your County Human Services Agency** (for CalFresh, CalWORKs, Medi‑Cal)

You may qualify for **Medi‑Cal** (California’s Medicaid program) or other health‑care help if you meet the income, residency, and citizenship/immigration rules that your county uses. Below is a simple guide to get you started.
## 1. Medi‑Cal (California Medicaid)

column3: Details

• U.S. citizens, lawful permanent residents, and many other qualified immigrants (e.g., refugees, asylees, DACA recipients).

Generally, your household income must be **≤ 138 % of the Federal Poverty Level (FPL)**. The exact dollar amount changes each year, so check the latest table on the **Medi‑Cal eligibility page** or ask your local social services office.
*If your income is higher, you might still get **Medi‑Cal “Buy‑Down”** (partial coverage) or qualify for **Covered California** subsidies.
Usually not counted, except for certain limited cases (e.g., large cash savings).

1. **Online** at [CoveredCA.com – Medi‑Cal Apply](https://www.coveredca.com/medicaid/).
2. **In person** at your county social services office (look up “County Social Services” + your county name).
3. **Phone**: Call 1‑800‑541‑5555 (Medi‑Cal Customer Service).

• Proof of California residency (driver’s license, utility bill, lease).
• Proof of income (pay stubs, unemployment benefits letter, SSI award letter, or self‑employment records).
• Proof of citizenship/immigration status (green card, visa, I‑94, or documentation of asylum/refugee status).
Most applications are processed within **15–30 days**. If additional info is needed, you’ll be contacted.
Some counties run their own eligibility centers and may ask for extra paperwork (e.g., proof of rent). Call your local office to confirm any special steps.

column1: ## 3. Step‑by‑Step How to Get Started
1. **Gather your paperwork** (list above).
2. **Visit your county’s Social Services website** – search “County Social Services + [your county]” (e.g., “Los Angeles County Social Services”).
3. **Create an online account** (most counties use **CalWIN** or **BenefitsCal**) and start the Medi‑Cal application.
4. **Submit the application** and upload copies of your documents.
5. **Watch for a response** – you’ll get a notice by mail, email, or phone within ~2 weeks.
6. **If approved**, you’ll receive a **Medi‑Cal ID card**; if you qualify for a different program (CHIP, Buy‑Down, etc.), the notice will explain the next steps.
7. **If denied or you need more help**, you can:
* Call the county office’s **Eligibility Hotline** (usually listed on the website).
* Request a **fair hearing** (you have the right to appeal).
* Reach out to a **local legal aid or community organization** for assistance (e.g., Legal Aid Society, California Rural Legal Assistance).
## 4. Tips & Things to Remember
- **Apply as soon as possible** – benefits can be retroactive to the first day of the month you applied, so you won’t lose coverage for the time you were unemployed.
- **Don’t wait for a “perfect” income level** – many programs have sliding scales; even a small change in income could still keep you eligible.
- **Keep copies** of everything you submit and note the date you sent it.
- **If you move to a different county**, you’ll need to re‑apply through the new county’s office.
- **You can be enrolled in more than one program** (e.g., Medi‑Cal + a charity‑care program) as long as you meet each program’s rules.

## How to Apply
### 1️⃣ Online (recommended)
1. Go to the **myEDD portal**: https://myedd.ca.gov/
2. Create a new account (you’ll need your EDD Customer Account Number, which is mailed to you after you start a claim).
3. Follow the on‑screen steps:
- Enter personal info.
- List your employers for the past 18 months.
- Provide your bank info for direct deposit.
4. Submit the application. You’ll get an email confirmation and a “Welcome” message with your UI claim number.
### 2️⃣ By Phone
- Call **UI Customer Service**: 1‑800‑300‑5616 (TDD/TTY: 1‑800‑815‑9387).
- An agent can start the claim for you and mail you the paper form if you prefer.
### 3️⃣ By Mail or Fax
1. Download **DE‑1101I** (English or Spanish).
2. Fill it out completely and attach copies of the documents above.
3. Mail or fax to the address/number on the form.
4. You can also drop it off at any **America’s Job Center of California** for free help.
### 4️⃣ In Person
- Visit your local **America’s Job Center** (no cost) for hands‑on assistance with the paper application or to get a computer for the online portal.

column1: ## Important Notes

## 1. Apply for CalFresh (food assistance)
### What you need to know
- **What it is:** Monthly cash benefit you can use to buy groceries.
- **Who can apply:** Any California resident ≥ 18 y/o; no citizenship requirement if you meet the “qualified immigrant” rules.
- **Eligibility basics:**
* Household income ≤ 200 % of the Federal Poverty Level (about $3,200/month for a single adult in 2025).
* You must have **little or no cash on hand** (≤ $200 for a single person).
### Steps to apply
1. **Gather documents** – you’ll need:
- Photo ID (driver’s license, state ID, or passport)
- Proof your job ended (lay‑off letter, final pay stub, termination email, or a written note with the last work date)
- Recent utility bill or rent statement (helps prove where you live)
- Bank‑statement or a statement that you have ≤ $200 in cash/assets (if asked)
2. **Apply online** – go to **[BenefitsCal.com](https://www.getcalfresh.org/en)** and select **CalFresh**.
- Fill out the short questionnaire.
- Upload the documents from step 1.
3. **County interview** – Within 1‑2 weeks the county will call you for a **phone interview** (or sometimes a video call). They’ll verify the info you entered.
4. **Decision** – You’ll get a letter or email with the result. If approved, you’ll receive an **EBT card** in the mail (usually 7‑10 days) and the first benefit amount within the next month.
5. **Expedited service** – Tell the interview‑er you need **emergency food help**. They can give you a **one‑time $200‑$300 cash advance** while your case is processed.
## 2. Apply for CalWORKs (if you have children or are pregnant)
### What it is
CalWORKs is California’s TANF (Temporary Assistance for Needy Families) program. It provides cash aid each month for:
- Food, rent, utilities, clothing, medical care, **and** other basic needs.
### Basic eligibility
- You must be a **California resident** with at least one dependent child (or you’re pregnant).
- Household income ≤ 200 % of the federal poverty level (similar to CalFresh).
- Must meet **asset limits** (generally ≤ $2,000 for a family, but many counties waive this for emergency cases).
### Steps
1. **Apply** – Same portal **[BenefitsCal.com](https://www.getcalfresh.org/en)**; choose **CalWORKs**.
2. **Provide documents** – Same as CalFresh plus:
- Birth certificates or school records for each dependent.
- Proof of pregnancy (if applicable).
3. **County interview** – Same timeline as CalFresh.
4. **Emergency cash** – Ask for “immediate short‑term help” during the interview. This can be given **within a few days** of approval.
## 3. Apply for Unemployment Insurance (UI)
Even though you’re focused on food now, filing for UI will give you cash flow for other bills.
1. **Go to** **[EDD.ca.gov/unemployment](https://edd.ca.gov/en/unemployment/)**.
2. **Create an account** and start the **“Apply for Unemployment”** wizard.
3. **Provide:**
- Social Security number
- Last employer’s name, address, and dates worked
- Reason you’re no longer working (lay‑off)
4. **Register for CalJOBS** (mandatory for UI).
5. **Certify each two weeks** after you’re approved to keep receiving payments.

column3: A **temporary cash benefit** for workers who lost their job—or had hours reduced—**through no fault of their own**.

**$40 – $450 per week** (the exact amount is based on your earnings during the “base period”).  Use the **[UI Benefits Calculator](https://edd.ca.gov/en/unemployment/benefit_calculator/)** to get an estimate.

column1: ## Basic Eligibility (same across the state)
You must be able to show **all** of the following:
1. **Worked enough wages** in the base period (the 12‑month period ending before you filed).
2. **Totally or partially unemployed** through no fault of your own (e.g., laid off, hours cut).
3. **Physically able** to work, **available** for work, and **actively looking** for work each week.
4. **Authorized to work** in the U.S. (U.S. citizen, permanent resident, or eligible non‑citizen).
5. Have a valid **Social Security number**.
> **Note:** Some counties have additional outreach resources or local job‑center requirements, so check your county’s American Job Center for any extra steps.

column1: ## How to **Maximize** Your UI Benefits
1. **Certify on time, every week** – Late certifications can delay or suspend payments.
2. **Report any earnings right away** – Even a few dollars earned must be reported; otherwise you risk an overpayment and possible penalties.

3. **Enroll in CalJOBS** and keep your profile up‑to‑date – This satisfies the “looking for work” rule and may give you higher weekly benefits if you qualify for **California Training Benefits** (you can take approved courses while receiving UI).
4. **Apply for other state assistance** while you receive UI:
* **CalFresh (food stamps)** – Income limits are higher when you’re on UI.
* **California’s Emergency Rental Assistance Program (ERAP)** – Helps with housing costs.
* **Medi‑Cal** – Low‑cost health coverage.
* **Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act (WIOA) programs** – Offer training vouchers and job placement services.
5. **Keep detailed records** of all job‑search activities, earnings, and any communications with EDD. This makes appeals easier if a decision seems wrong.

6. **Check county‑specific resources** – Many counties run additional workshops on resume building, interview skills, and rapid re‑employment; attending can improve your chances of finding work sooner, which may also qualify you for **re‑employment assistance** programs later.

column1: ## When Things Go Wrong
* **Overpayment notice (DE 1444)** – If you receive benefits you weren’t eligible for, EDD will send a notice. You have the right to **appeal**. Continue certifying while the appeal is pending.
* **Denial of benefits** – You’ll receive a **Notice of Determination (DE 1080CZ)** and an **Appeal Form (DE 1000M)**. File an appeal within **30 days** and keep certifying.
For any questions, you can:
* Log into **UI Online** and use the “Ask EDD” feature.
* Call the UI Customer Service line: **1‑800‑300‑5616** (M‑F, 8 a.m.–5 p.m. PT).
* Visit your local **America’s Job Center of California** for in‑person help.

Start the UI application today, keep your certifications up to date, and explore the additional programs listed above. If you need more personalized help, a staff member at your county’s Job Center can walk you through each step.

Q_023,I’m getting a severance and might do part-time gig work. Can I still get unemployment and also Medi-Cal?,"## Quick answer
Yes – you can **apply for both unemployment insurance (UI) and Medi‑Cal** even if you receive a severance payment and plan to do part‑time gig work.

You’ll need to report the severance and any earnings from the gig work on your UI claim, and you’ll need to show your household income when you apply for Medi‑Cal. Both programs will look at the same income information, but they use it in different ways.
## How unemployment works after a severance

column3: Why it matters
The California Employment Development Department (EDD) treats severance pay like regular wages. When you certify each week, you must tell EDD how much severance you received that week.
If the severance amount is low enough or spread out over several weeks, you may still meet the earnings test for UI.

You can work part‑time and still receive UI as long as you are **“available, willing, and able”** to work full‑time and your earnings stay below the weekly earnings limit (about 25 % of your weekly benefit amount).
Not reporting severance or gig earnings can lead to overpayments that you’ll have to pay back, and it could affect future benefits.
Log in to **UI Online**, go to “Report a Change,” and enter the amount of severance and any gig earnings for that week.

column1: **Next steps for unemployment**
1. **Apply** (if you haven’t already) at the EDD website: <https://edd.ca.gov/en/unemployment/>.
2. **Register** in CalJOBS (required for UI).
3. **Certify weekly** – report severance and gig earnings each week.
4. **Keep records** of pay stubs, severance letters, and any 1099‑G forms you receive.
Processing usually takes **about 3 weeks** for the first payment, but it can be longer if you have a severance or variable earnings.
## Medi‑Cal basics

column3: What it means for you
If your household income is at or below 138 % of the federal poverty level (FPL) you qualify for **no‑cost Medi‑Cal**. If it’s higher, you may still qualify for **Medi‑Cal with a share of cost**.
All money you receive—salary, severance, gig work, unemployment benefits—counts toward the household income test.

column2: **No‑cost coverage for children and pregnant people**
column3: Even higher‑income families may get free coverage for kids or pregnant individuals.

Each county runs its own **Medi‑Cal enrollment office** and may have slightly different paperwork or outreach programs. The basic eligibility rules are the same, but the **documents they ask for can differ**.

column1: ### How to apply for Medi‑Cal
1. **Gather documents** (see table below).
2. **Apply online** at <https://www.coveredca.com/> (choose “Apply for Medi‑Cal”) **or** call your **County Social Services Agency** (find contact at <https://www.cdss.ca.gov/calworks#main-content>).
3. **Submit the application** – most counties process new applications within **45 days** (often sooner).
4. **Wait for a determination** – you’ll get a letter or email with your eligibility and any share‑of‑cost amount.
5. **Choose a Medi‑Cal health plan** (your county will give you a list).
### Documents you’ll typically need

column3: Example documents
Driver’s license, state ID, passport
Utility bill, lease, mail addressed to you
Recent pay stubs, severance letter, 1099‑G (UI), gig platform earnings statements, bank statements
Birth certificates or school enrollment for children, marriage certificate if applying as a couple
Green card, work permit, or other status documents

column1: *If you can’t get a specific document, write a brief letter explaining why and include any alternative proof you have.*
## Can you get both at the same time?
- **Yes.** Receiving UI does **not** stop you from getting Medi‑Cal.
- UI benefits are **considered income** when the county calculates your Medi‑Cal eligibility, but many families qualify for Medi‑Cal even with UI because the income limits are relatively high.
- **Tell both agencies** about the severance and gig earnings; they will each use the information in their own formulas.

column1: ## Tips to keep everything on track
- **Report changes promptly** – any new gig earnings, a change in severance schedule, or a change in household size should be reported to both EDD and your county Medi‑Cal office within **5 days**.
- **Keep copies** of all letters, emails, and screenshots (e.g., an email from your former employer confirming your last work day).
- **Ask for help** – most counties have **“application assistance”** or **“phone help lines”** that can walk you through the forms.
- **Don’t wait** – you can apply for UI, Medi‑Cal, and CalFresh all at once. The agencies will tell you if you need more information.

- **CalFresh –** Call 1‑877‑847‑3663 or start an online application at <https://www.getcalfresh.org/>.

Q_024,Rent is due next weke and I hvae high utilities. Is theer emergency help while I apply for Unempolyment Insurance?,"## You’re Not Alone – Help Is Available While You Wait for Unemployment
Losing a job is stressful, especially when rent and utility bills are coming due.
You can **apply for unemployment insurance (UI) now** and **look for emergency assistance** for rent and energy at the same time. Below is a simple guide to get you started.
## 1️⃣ Start Your Unemployment Claim

column3: Why it matters
Required to verify identity.

column2: **Proof of recent work & wages** (pay stubs, W‑2, or an online earnings summary)
column3: Shows you earned enough in the “base period” (last 18 months).

column2: **Proof you are able and looking for work** (job‑search log, email confirmations)
column3: UI requires you to be “available for work.”

column2: **Bank account info** (for the EDD debit card)
column3: Benefits are deposited on a Money Network debit card.

column1: **How to apply**
1. Go to the **Employment Development Department (EDD) website**: <https://edd.ca.gov/en/unemployment/>
2. Click **“File a New Claim.”**
3. Follow the step‑by‑step prompts; it takes about 15‑20 minutes.
4. After you submit, the first payment usually arrives **within 3 weeks** (often sooner if all documents are complete).
*Tip:* You can start the claim even if you’re not sure you’ll be eligible. EDD will let you know.
## 2️⃣ Emergency Rent Assistance (While You Wait)
### What’s Available?
- **California Emergency Rental Assistance Program (ERAP)** – money to pay rent, security deposits, or utility arrears.
- **Local 211 referrals** – many counties run their own short‑term rent‑help funds.
- **HUD‑certified housing counselors** – free advice and sometimes direct referrals.
### Basic Eligibility (same across most counties)

column3: Typical Details
Must live in the state.

column2: **Household income ≤ 80 % of the area median income** (exact limit varies by county)
column3: County X may use 75 %, County Y may use 80 %.

column2: **Rent or utility bill overdue** (usually within the last 60 days)
column3: Shows you have an immediate need.
Lease, rent receipt, or utility statement.

column2: **Proof of identity** (driver’s license or state ID)
column3: Confirms who you are.

column1: ### Steps to Apply
1. **Call 211** (or dial **211** on your phone) – the operator will connect you to the agency that runs the emergency rent program in your county.

Q_027,"I was laid off, have kdis, and savings are low. For food stamps, can I get faster help and how does UI or severance affect eligibility? I might move countise soon to live with my mom to save money—what changes?","## Quick guide to getting **CalFresh (food stamps)** right after a lay‑off

column3: Simple explanation

column2: **Can you get CalFresh while you are on unemployment (UI)?**
column3: Yes.  UI benefits are counted as income, but you can still qualify as long as the total household income stays under the CalFresh limit.  Getting CalFresh will **not** reduce your UI payment.

A one‑time severance payment is treated as income for the month you receive it.  You must report it on the CalFresh application; it may lower the benefit amount for that month, but you can still be eligible.

Most counties schedule an eligibility interview **within 1‑2 weeks** after you apply.  After the interview, a decision is usually made within **30 days**.  If you are approved, the first benefit month can start **as soon as the first day of the following month** (often within a week of approval).

column2: **What if you move to another county?**
column3: CalFresh is administered by each county’s Department of Social Services.  When you move, you must **transfer or re‑apply** in the new county.  The basic rules are the same, but paperwork and interview times can differ.  Call the new county office as soon as you know the move date.

column1: ## 1. How to apply for CalFresh
1. **Start online** – go to **[BenefitsCal.com](https://www.getcalfresh.org/en)** and click **“Apply”.**
2. **Create a myEDD account** (if you haven’t already) to file UI claims and to use the same email address for both programs.
3. **Submit the online application.**
4. **County interview** – Your county social services office will call you within 1‑2 weeks for a phone interview (or may ask you to come in).
5. **Provide documents** (see list below).
6. **Decision** – You will receive a notice by mail or online. If approved, the first benefit month starts at the beginning of the next month.

## 2. How UI (Unemployment Insurance) works with CalFresh

column3: What to do
Register on **UI Online** (myEDD) as soon as you are laid off. You need a valid email address.
When the county asks for your current income, tell them the weekly UI amount you receive.
If you receive a lump‑sum severance, list it as “other income” for the month you get it. It may lower that month’s CalFresh benefit, but you’ll still get help for the rest of the year.
If your UI payment changes (higher or lower), call the CalFresh office or update the online portal within 7 days.

column1: ## 3. Moving to a new county (e.g., to live with your mom)
1. **Tell your current county** you are moving. They will close your case and send a transfer file.
2. **Contact the new county** (search “[County] CalFresh”) **within 10 days** of the move. Ask for a “transfer of case” or start a fresh application if the file is not transferred.
3. **Bring the same documents** listed above, plus proof of the new address (lease, utility bill, or a letter from your mom).
4. **Timing** – The new county will schedule its own interview. Expect a similar 1‑2‑week wait, so start early to avoid a gap in benefits.
> *Note:* Each county may have slightly different waiting times or office hours, but the eligibility rules are set by the state and are the same everywhere.

1. **Apply for UI** on myEDD (UI Online).
2. **Apply for CalFresh** at BenefitsCal.com.
3. Gather the documents listed above; keep digital copies if possible.
4. Mark your calendar for the **phone interview** (you’ll get a call; add the number 1‑800‑300‑5616 to your contacts).

### You’re not alone

Losing a job is stressful, but California has a network of programs to keep you and your children fed, housed, and healthy. Start the applications today, keep your paperwork ready, and let the county staff guide you through the interview. If you run into a roadblock, call **211** (dial 2‑1‑1) for free, local help.
